a-chord-and-two-feet.alt: Circle omega with centre O and triangle ABC inscribed, A at the top. Chord XY is horizontal and passes through P on AB and Q on AC, with XP = 64, PQ = 56 and QY = 48. The tangent at A is parallel to XY, and the radius OA meets XY at right angles at its midpoint M.

a-corner-of-forty-five-degrees.alt: A regular 20-sided polygon in its circle, with centre O. A triangle joins three of its vertices. Two of them are 5 sides apart, and the arc between them, made of 5 sides, is highlighted: it makes a right angle, 90 degrees, at O. The third vertex lies on the long arc, and the angle of the triangle there is 45 degrees, half of 90 degrees.

a-hub-for-four-points.alt: The plane through line PQ and the point A, after B has been rotated about line PQ into this plane, onto the side away from A, to the point B'. P and Q lie on the line 8 apart. A is 3 from the line with foot P, and B' is 7 from the line with foot Q, both at right angles. The straight segment AB' crosses the line at X, and AB' squared is 8 squared plus 10 squared, which is 164.

a-lone-solution.alt: The complex plane, with the circle of radius 20 centred at 3 - 8i. Four segments of length 10 and the same direction start on the real axis at k. For k = -16 the segment touches the circle at its midpoint. For k = 0 it lies inside the circle, so there is no solution. For k = 9 its far end lies on the circle. For k = 15 it crosses the circle once.

a-parallel-radius.alt: Triangle ABC with BC = 7, CA = 20 and AB = 15, and its circumcircle with centre O. The foot H of the altitude from A lies on line BC beyond B, so the angle at B is obtuse. Segment AO is parallel to BC and so perpendicular to the altitude AH, and angle B exceeds angle C by 90 degrees.

a-point-on-the-leg.alt: Isosceles triangle ABC with AB = AC and a 40 degree angle at A. Point D on side AC has BD = BC, with tick marks on BD and BC. The angles at B and C of triangle ABC are 70 degrees, angle DBC is 40 degrees, and the highlighted angle ABD is 30 degrees.

a-point-sent-round-two-centres.alt: Triangle PAB with PA = 4, PB = 6 and AB squared = 28. Rotating P about A through theta gives Q, and rotating Q back through theta about B gives R. The same two rotations send A to A', which is B's rotation of A. PR and AA' are parallel and equal, both of length 7, because the two rotations together form a translation.

a-point-sliding-along-an-arc.alt: Two equal circles with centres A and B, each passing through the other's centre, meet at E. C is the second point where line AB meets the circle centred at A, and P lies on arc CE away from B. Triangle ABE is equilateral with a 60 degree angle at E, triangle AEP is isosceles with AE = AP and apex angle theta at A, and segment EP is highlighted.

a-sphere-on-a-box.alt: Vertical section of the box through the top-face diagonal AC, drawn as rectangle A, C, Q, P with AC = 30 and AP = 25. The circle with centre O and radius 17 passes through A and C and touches PQ at its midpoint T; M is the midpoint of AC, with AM = 15, MO = 8 and OA = OT = 17, and triangle AMO is shaded with its right angle at M.

a-square-on-the-move.alt: The hexagon O(0,0), A(2,0), B(9,3), C(9,5), D(7,5), E(0,2) is the swept region. It is split by F(2,2) into the starting square OAFE, the parallelogram ABCF swept by the right side, and the parallelogram EFCD swept by the top side. A dashed segment runs from O to G(7,3), the path of the lower-left corner.

closer-to-the-line.alt: Square ABCD with side 20, and the line MN through the midpoint M of BC and the point N on CD. The favourable region is shaded. On A's side of MN it is the pentagon M, Q, R, S, N, and on C's side it is the triangle M, N, P. The rays from A through Q and S are dashed.

colours-on-a-cut-up-decagon.alt: A convex 10-gon divided into triangles by 7 non-crossing diagonals. The shaded triangle has two polygon sides, va and vb, so no diagonal leaves v and the third side ab is a drawn diagonal. Removing v leaves a triangulated 9-gon in which ab is a side.

diagonals-of-a-leaning-parallelogram.alt: Parallelogram ABCD with AB = 12 and height 5, the point E on line AB beyond B with BE = 12, and E' the reflection of E in line DC. Segments BD and CE are marked equal, and the dashed segment AE' has length 26.

down-up-and-across.alt: Coordinate plane with the x-axis and the line y = 10. A = (0, 3) is reflected in the x-axis to A' = (0, -3), and B = (24, 5) is reflected in y = 10 to B' = (24, 15). The straight segment from A' to B', of length 30, crosses the x-axis at P = (4, 0) and the line y = 10 at Q = (52/3, 10). The highlighted path runs from A to P to Q to B.

feet-on-the-sides.alt: Acute triangle ABC drawn for h = 30, with base BC horizontal. The altitude AD from A to BC has length 20, the altitude BE from B to CA has length 21, and the altitude CF from C to AB is shown. All three feet lie inside their sides and are marked with right angles.

fencing-two-colours.alt: The lower-bound construction drawn small: three red points, labelled R and drawn in the accent colour, and three blue points, labelled B, alternate around a circle, and one more blue point lies off the circle. Every chord joining neighbouring points on the circle joins two colours, so some line must cross it. The highlighted line crosses exactly two sides of the hexagon formed by the six points, and no line can cross more than two.

four-of-twelve-vertices.alt: A regular dodecagon ABCDEFGHIJKL with centre O, drawn with the chord AF across the top. Quadrilateral ABCF is shaded. The centre O lies below AF, outside ABCF. Segments OA, OB, OC and OF cut the pentagon OABCF into triangles OAB and OBC, each with a 30 degree angle at O, and OCF, with a right angle at O. Triangle OAF, shaded grey, has a 150 degree angle at O, so it has the same area as triangle OAB, which is 30. The quadrilateral is the pentagon with triangle OAF removed, so its area is 30 + 30 + 60 - 30 = 90.

four-orthogonal-quadrilaterals.alt: A kite-shaped convex quadrilateral ABCD with P, Q, R, S on sides AB, BC, CD, DA. The segments PR and QS cross at O and split ABCD into four quadrilaterals, and in each the diagonal through O is perpendicular to the opposite diagonal: OA is perpendicular to PS, OB to PQ, OC to QR and OD to RS, marked with right angles. The circle through P, Q, R and S is dashed. Adapted from Beyond the Incenter, Problem 96.

four-sides-and-an-area.alt: Convex quadrilateral ABCD with AB = 2, BC = 9, CD = 6 and DA = 7. The diagonal AC is highlighted, and right angles are marked at B and D, so AC is the hypotenuse of both triangles ABC and ACD.

half-in-common.alt: Triangle ABC with BC = 13, CA = 10 and AB = 5, its incircle with centre I, and the dashed triangle A'B'C' obtained by the half-turn about I. Each side of A'B'C' is parallel to a side of ABC and cuts a small corner off ABC; the shaded hexagon left over is the common region, and its area is half that of ABC.

halfway-between-two-frames.alt: The set of midpoints drawn as a shaded rectangular frame. The outer rectangle RSTU measures 7 by 4, with R at (10, 5) and T at (17, 9), and the unshaded inner rectangle EFGH measures 3 by 2, with E at (12, 6) and G at (15, 8).

medians-meeting-on-the-circle.alt: Triangle ABC with AB = 5, BC = 10 and CA = 13, an example of the condition. Its incircle has centre I and touches BC, CA and AB at Ta, Tb and Tc; the two tangents from A are marked x and the tangent from C along CA is marked z. The median from A to the midpoint Ma of BC is dashed; the centroid G, where the medians meet, lies on it and on the incircle.

nineteen-planted-plots.alt: A 5 by 5 field of 1 m square plots. Six plots are left empty and shaded: the centre plot, the four plots diagonally next to it, and the middle plot of the bottom edge. No two empty plots share a side. The fencing, highlighted, runs round the outside of the field except along the bottom side of the empty edge plot, and round each of the five inner empty plots. It has length 22 + 5 times 4 = 42 metres.

parallels-through-k.alt: Triangle ABC with K on BC beyond C. Through K, KP is parallel to AB with BP = BK, and KQ is parallel to AC with CQ = CK. The circle through K, P and Q meets AK again at T. The auxiliary point D, with triangle CTD similar to triangle CQA, is joined to A, B, C and T, and the dashed segments AP, AQ, BT, CT, PT and QT show the two similar pairs used in the proof. Adapted from Beyond the Incenter, Problem 86.

segments-between-segments.alt: Trapezium ABCD with AB = 4 at the top and CD = 6 at the bottom. The diagonals of ABCD meet at a point on the highlighted segment l2, of length 24/5, which runs between the legs AD and BC parallel to AB. The diagonals of the trapezium with parallel sides CD and l2 meet on l3, of length 16/3, and the diagonals of the trapezium with parallel sides l2 and l3 meet on l4. Each new segment lies between the two before it, so the segments close in on one limiting segment.

six-points-and-one-more.alt: A close-up of side AB = 14 of the regular hexagon, with P on the short arc AB above it. The lines from P towards the far vertices E and D cross AB at U and V, with AU = 6, UV = 1 and VB = 7. At P the angle APB of 150 degrees is split into 60, 30 and 60 degrees.

sixty-at-both-ends.alt: Equilateral triangle ABE drawn dashed, with D on side AE and C on side BE. The quadrilateral ABCD has 60 degree angles at A and B; the shaded triangle DEC that is cut off has a 60 degree angle at E, with ED = x and EC = y. In the case drawn AB = 12, x = 3, y = 8 and CD = 7.

sixty-degrees-at-a.alt: Two triangles share side AB = 8 and the 60 degree angle at A. The third vertex lies on the same ray from A, at C with AC = 3 or at C' with AC' = 5. Both points are at distance 7 from B, on a dashed arc centred at B.

three-areas-in-a-hexagon.alt: Regular hexagon ABCDEF with a point P inside it, joined to all six vertices. Triangles PAB, PBC and PCD carry their areas 7, 10 and 15. The triangles PAB, PCD and PEF on alternate sides are shaded. The sides AB, CD and EF are extended to form a large equilateral triangle around the hexagon; the distances from P to its three sides add up to its height, so the shaded triangles make half of the hexagon. The opposite sides BC and EF are parallel, so triangles PBC and PEF make a third of it, and the hexagon has area 72.

three-chords.alt: Part of the parabola y = x squared, with the triangle whose vertices have x-coordinates a = 0, b = 2 and c = 3. Its sides have slopes a + b = 2, a + c = 3 and b + c = 5, which is the sum of the x-coordinates at each pair of ends.

three-points-on-the-base.alt: Triangle ABC in its circumcircle with centre O. On BC lie the midpoint E, the foot D of the bisector from A, and, beyond C, the foot F of the altitude from A, with DE = 3, DF = 12 and AF = 16. The bisector AD is extended to N, the lowest point of the circle, directly below E with NE = 4. The shaded right triangles DEN and DFA are similar, and dashed segments join O to N and to B.

three-rows-of-circles.alt: Triangle ABC with side BC along the bottom. Ten circles of radius 1 sit in a row along BC without overlapping, each touching BC and the next one; the first touches AB and is centred at B', and the last touches CA and is centred at C'. A circle of radius 1 centred at A' touches AB and CA. The triangle A'B'C', with B'C' = 18, C'A' = 20 and A'B' = 34, has its sides parallel to those of ABC at distance 1; it has area 144 and inradius 4, and ABC has inradius 5 and area 225.

three-triangles-from-one-point.alt: Square with B at the origin, C = (12, 0) on the x-axis and A = (0, 12) on the y-axis, and the fourth vertex D. Point P = (10/3, 5) lies below the diagonal AC. Triangles PAB and PBC are shaded with areas 20 and 30, and triangle PAC is highlighted with area 22.

through-two-vertices-and-the-incentre.alt: Acute triangle ABC inscribed in a circle of radius 13, with BC = 24. M is the midpoint of the arc BC not containing A, and the bisector AM passes through the incentre I. The highlighted circle with centre M passes through B, I and C, and MB = MI = MC.

twenty-seven-points.alt: An oblique view of the cube whose corners have coordinates 0 and 2, with the nine points of its bottom face marked. A triangle PQR with vertices P = (2, 0, 1), Q = (0, 1, 2) and R = (2, 2, 2) is drawn above its shaded shadow P'Q'R' on the bottom face z = 0, and dashed vertical segments join each vertex to its shadow.

two-circles-on-the-legs.alt: Trapezium ABCD with AB parallel to CD. The circles on the legs AD and BC as diameters, centred at their midpoints M and N, touch at P on the midline MN. Segments PA = 75, PD = 100, PB = 65 and PC = 156 make right angles APD and BPC. A dashed circle of radius 60 centred at P touches all four sides: P is the centre of the inscribed circle.

two-orbits.alt: Two concentric circles with centre O and radii 16 and 39, the outer one shown as an arc, with A on the inner circle and B on the outer. At the moment contact begins, angle AOB is 120 degrees and AB = 49. Segment AB just touches the disc of radius r around O, at the foot F of the perpendicular from O, with a right angle at F.

two-polygons-one-circle.alt: Circle with a regular 12-gon and a regular pentagon inscribed, sharing the vertex A at the top. Each of the 16 points of S is labelled with its clockwise arc in degrees from A: multiples of 30 and of 72. The pentagon is dashed. One admissible polygon is drawn in bold, visiting 0, 30, 72, 90, 144, 150, 216, 240, 288, 300 and back to A.

two-rods-in-a-square-frame.alt: Square ABCD of side s, with P on AB, Q on BC, R on CD and S on DA, drawn for s = 24. The diagonals of quadrilateral PQRS are PR = 25 and QS = 31. Its area is half the size of the cross product of these two diagonals.

The extreme case, a square with side 31 over root 2. P is at A, Q is at B and S is at D, so QS is the diagonal BD with length 31. R lies on CD with PR = 25. The shaded quadrilateral PQRS is a right trapezium with area 372.

two-turns-on-repeat.alt: The robot's path from O: six moves of 1 metre, starting north, with turns of 100 and 140 degrees clockwise in turn. P1 to P5 are its positions after 1 to 5 moves, and the sixth move ends at O. The moves meet at P1 at an angle of 80 degrees. The points O, P2 and P4, reached after 0, 2 and 4 moves, form an equilateral triangle with side 2 sin 40 degrees, drawn dashed with its sides highlighted, because each pair of moves is the previous pair rotated by 120 degrees.

two-whole-squares.alt: The ellipse x squared plus xy plus y squared equals 360, centred at the origin O, with its long axis along the line y = -x. A and B lie on it with a right angle at O, drawn for OA squared = 288 and OB squared = 480. A right-angle turn of OA changes the sign of s, so the two squared distances are 360 over 1 + s and 360 over 1 - s.

where-the-circle-touches.alt: Triangle ABC with AB = 6, AC = 10 and BC = 8 times root 5 minus 8, about 9.89. The bisector from A meets BC at D. A circle through A touches BC at D and crosses AB at P and AC at Q. The chord PQ is parallel to BC and passes through the incentre I, so I and PQ are at the same height above BC.

where-the-coin-cannot-reach.alt: Triangle ABC with BC = 20, CA = 15 and AB = 7, its incircle with centre I and radius 2, and the dashed inner triangle A'B'C', the image of ABC under the homothety at I with ratio 1/2. The coin of radius 1 is drawn pushed into each corner, centred at the vertices A', B' and C' of the inner triangle. At each vertex of ABC the shaded kite has corners at the vertex, the two points where the coin touches the sides, and the coin's centre; the part of the kite outside the coin is never covered. Dashed segments join I to C and to the incircle's points of contact on BC and CA, outlining the incircle's kite at C, which is twice the size of the coin's kite at C.

whole-number-distances.alt: Isosceles triangle ACE with CA = CE = h, drawn for h = 144. B is the midpoint of AE, with AB = BE = 90 and a right angle between BC and AE. D lies on side CE, AD bisects angle CAE, and CD = h squared over (h + 180). CB bisects angle ACE, so E is the reflection of A in line BC.
